## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ258** (PubChem CID [59396138](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/59396138))

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The call was driven by potent, reproducible large-nucleus polyploidy at 0.1, 1 and 3 uM with frac_large_nucleus z=+98.8 to +106.7 and nuc_area z=+38.0 to +46.4, replicated at 1 uM, and a negative threshold at 0.01 uM. The microscopist visual call and 9/10 Aurora kinase inhibitor atlas neighbours correctly dominated over the DNA-damage runner-up.

The high-dose 30 uM well with tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.9 and act_glcm_contrast z=+22.6 briefly raised microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer hypotheses. It was correctly downweighted because mid/low doses showed the clean nuclear phenotype without that cytoskeletal texture, consistent with high-dose toxicity/condensation rather than a primary microtubule mechanism.

Sampling low-mid doses plus a 1 uM replicate and the atlas comparison was decisive; imaging alone could not resolve Aurora A vs B or mononuclear polyploidy vs binucleation from failed cytokinesis, which is why phospho-marker and live-imaging follow-up is needed.

What was right:
- Prioritized potent reproducible frac_large_nucleus and nuc_area increase across 0.1-3 uM with 1 uM replicate confirmation as polyploidy from failed mitosis/cytokinesis
- Used 0.01 uM negative and lower density vs DMSO to establish a potency threshold rather than nonspecific toxicity
- Weighted describe_phenotype Aurora call and 9/10 Aurora atlas neighbours over weak DNA-damage and microtubule alternatives

What was wrong or missed:
- High-dose 30 uM tubulin/actin texture spike transiently inflated microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer probabilities before mid-dose bridging showed it was off-target/high-dose effect
- Did not resolve Aurora A vs Aurora B subtype or prove binucleation vs endoreduplication from imaging features alone

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry with pHH3-Ser10 and p-Aurora staining plus live-cell imaging of mitosis/cytokinesis to confirm polyploid binucleation from failed cytokinesis and to distinguish Aurora A vs B target engagement versus microtubule poisons.

- PMID [30540594](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30540594/): Aurora kinase B inhibitor barasertib (AZD1152) inhibits glucose metabolism in gastric cancer cells. *Anticancer Drugs* (2019) — Barasertib (AZD1152) is an Aurora kinase B inhibitor, exemplifying the reference class matched by the atlas.
